81	**What the core refuses**, each sentence naming the value:
82	- `module` failing `model_graphic::check_name`.
83	- `title`, `category` or `app_version` that is not a string, or a `description` that is neither a string nor null.
84	- A first file that is not exactly `<module>.js`.
85	- Any other file not `fonts/<n>` or `assets/<n>`, where `<n>` must be non-empty, at most 255 bytes, and hold no `/`. Any other character is legalised, never refused (below).
86	- A path given twice.
87	- Sizes that do not sum to `len`.
88	- An archive over `u32::MAX` bytes (there is no Zip64).
89	- I/O failures.
90	
91	**The archive:**
92	- Stored (method 0), version needed 10, made-by `0x031E`, flag bit 11 (UTF-8 names).
93	- DOS time 0 and date `0x0021` (1980-01-01), so the bytes are deterministic.
94	- No extra fields and no directory entries; external attributes `0o100644 << 16`.
95	- `manifest.json` first, then the files in the order given, then the central directory and the EOCD.
96	
97	**The in-package name** (G-46 (c)). A legal `<n>` is non-empty, at most 255 bytes, does not begin with `.`, and holds no `/`, `\`, `:` or control scalar (U+0000–U+001F, U+007F–U+009F). The module's entry is always `<module>.js`. For `fonts/` and `assets/`, each folder on its own:
98	- A legal `<n>` is kept as it is, and the legal names are claimed first, in the order given.
99	- Then each illegal `<n>`, in the order given, is legalised: each run of `\`, `:` or control scalars becomes one `-`, and leading `.`s are dropped; an empty result is `file`.
100	- A legalised name already claimed takes `-2`, `-3`, … before its last `.` (G-23 (c)'s form), the stem cut by whole scalars to stay within 255 bytes.
101	- `a:b.ttf` → `fonts/a-b.ttf`; `red\dot.png` → `assets/red-dot.png`; `a:b.ttf` beside a legal `a-b.ttf` → `fonts/a-b-2.ttf`.
102	
103	**`manifest.json`** is pretty JSON with a trailing newline, in this key order: `{"fjgraphic": 1, "module", "title", "category", "description", "app_version", "files": [{"path", "name", "size", "sha256"}…]}`. `path` is the in-package path; `name` is the file's name in its project folder (`<module>.js`, the font's, the asset's), which is how a module's `asset(name)` still resolves after a renamed entry is imported. `sha256` is lowercase hex, and the manifest does not list itself.

134	## Approach
135	1. **Spec §11 G-46, written before any code, in `graphics.md` with its README row.**
136	   - **(a) The door.** Export… sits at the sheet's far left, with From File… to its right. It is enabled when a graphic is chosen and compiles. It opens an `NSSavePanel` as a sheet on the browser, named `<module>.fjgraphic`. The browser stays up; the result or the refusal goes in `graphicbrowser.message`.
137	   - **(b) The usage rule.**
138	     - Build a fresh library: the bundled faces, then the project's fonts, then its assets. Compile the module against it.
139	     - Draw each frame (svg, then rasterize at the meta size, else the canvas) with default props. That is every frame up to 900; past that, 900 evenly spaced frames.
140	     - Then draw the variants, one at a time with every other prop at its default: each `enum` option other than the default, and each boolean's opposite. Take them in schema order, at most 32, over 30 evenly spaced frames each.
141	     - Pack every project font blob and asset the engine selected, measured, fell back to or resolved. A bundled face is never packed.
142	     - A frame that throws is skipped and counted. String and asset props are sampled only at their defaults.
143	   - **(c) The format,** as in Interfaces. Its paths mirror `graphics/`, so a later import is a copy. A project font or asset whose name the package path cannot hold (`\`, `:`, a control character, a leading `.`) is never refused at export: the core legalises its in-package name by Interfaces' rule, and the manifest's `name` keeps the project's, so an import can restore it and `asset(name)` still resolves. A font is found by family, never by file name, so its renamed entry changes no picture.
144	   - **(d) The UTI** is exported only; the app does not open a `.fjgraphic`.
145	   - **(e) `export_graphic`** runs off main, and is ask-first under AI-7's own criterion: it writes a file where the model chose.
146	   - **(f) Import is not built.** It is filed as an issue when the phase closes.
147	2. **The graphic crate.** Each closure calls usvg first — `select_font`, the fallback selector or `image_kind` — and only afterwards locks the usage set, for its own insert, because a nested SVG asset re-enters on the same thread. `tests/usage.rs`, with `common::fonts()`, checks:
148	   - Anton drawn records Anton's index; `serif` records Source Serif 4's; a missing family records nothing.
149	   - A fallback records both faces. Use a character Anton lacks: drawn in a library of Anton alone it draws nothing, and in Anton + Source Sans 3 it draws.
150	   - `measure_text` alone records its face.
151	   - A drawn PNG href is recorded; a non-image asset and a missing href are not.
152	   - A nested SVG asset's text records its face.
153	   - A faceless blob at index 0 moves Anton to index 1.
154	   - Usage accumulates across calls and is separate per library.
155	3. **The core.**
156	   - The CRC is CRC-32 IEEE: a reflected table, with init and xorout `0xFFFFFFFF`.
157	   - `tests/graphic_package.rs` uses its own zip reader (EOCD → central directory → local headers), a bitwise CRC (the check value `"123456789"` → `0xCBF43926`) and `sha2`. It checks:
158	     - each entry's order and bytes, its CRC, both size fields, flag bit 11 and the 1980 date;
159	     - the manifest's text, its key order and its checksums;
160	     - that two writes are byte-identical;
161	     - each refusal, with nothing written for an input refusal;
162	     - the in-package names: `fonts/a:b.ttf` → `fonts/a-b.ttf`, `assets/red\dot.png` → `assets/red-dot.png`, a control-character run → one `-`, a leading `.` dropped, `fonts/:` → `fonts/-`, `fonts/..` → `fonts/file`; `fonts/a:b.ttf` given before a legal `fonts/a-b.ttf` still yields `a-b.ttf` for the legal one and `a-b-2.ttf` for the renamed one; each manifest `name` is the given name; a legal name is unchanged.
163	   - Finish with `cargo fmt` and `make lint`.
164	4. **The ReelCore toll, landed and gated alone.**
165	   - **Payment 1, the byte-buffer helpers.** Add `withByteBuffer` and `withMutableByteBuffer` to `CoreValues.swift`. Rewrite the seven inline sites in `ReelCore.swift`: `withByteBuffer` at `ReelAV1.config`, `ReelWebM.add`/`addVideo`, `GraphicLibrary.addFont`/`addAsset`; `withMutableByteBuffer(&data)` at `ReelAV1.stripTemporalDelimiters` and `withMutableByteBuffer(&head)` at `ReelAV1.brandAV01`, which keep writing in place. The pointers, their mutability and the `rc_*` calls stay the same; no `UnsafeMutablePointer(mutating:)` anywhere.
166	   - **Payment 2, the `extension ReelOp` docs.** These seven sites save about 17 lines; `usage()` and `ReelGraphicPackage` add about 20. So `coreSchemas()`'s and `coreNames()`'s docs are cut to their contracts: what each answers, where it comes from (`rc_op_schemas` / `rc_op_names`), and that empty means the core failed. Their rationale paragraphs go word for word into the `ReelCore.swift` entry of `app-file-history.md`: why the FFI rather than a Swift copy, why empty is a catastrophe, and why the member stayed in this file. No code changes.
167	   - Each payment is a pure change, gated alone by `make typecheck` (0 errors, the 4 baseline warnings), and recorded with its before and after `wc -l`.
168	   - Only then add `usage()` and `ReelGraphicPackage`. If the file is still over 788 after them, stop and report it; do not relax the cap.
169	5. **`GraphicStore` and `GraphicPackageJob`.**
170	   - **The factories** read:
171	     - the meta: title, category and description through `GraphicCatalog`; the size and the length through `AgentServer.metaWhole`, as `render_graphic` does;
172	     - the module's bytes: `scan.modules[name].bytes`, or the template's file;
173	     - the library: `makeIndexedLibrary()`. A template gets a library of `bundledFontURLs` alone: every entry nil, no assets.
174	   - **`write`:**
175	     1. Compile at `GraphicRegistry.offlineBudgetMs`. A failure is G-45 (f)'s sentence, labelled `graphics/<name>.js` or `the template "<name>"`.
176	     2. Draw 1(b)'s frames through `AgentServer.graphicContext`. The variants come from `GraphicSchema(describeJSON:schema:)`.
177	     3. Map the usage to files: a font index to `fonts/<its file name>`, an asset to `assets/<name>`, both as project-relative paths. The core picks the in-package names; `GraphicPackageResult.files` is read from the manifest it answers.

262	RC_PROOF_APP=release python3 tools/proof/graphics_menu_proof.py     # covers: Export… in the sheet (M33–M37)
263	RC_PROOF_APP=release python3 tools/proof/graphic_browser_proof.py   # covers: export_graphic's package, the usage rule, legalised names, refusals, ten identifiers

266	python3 tools/proof/graphics_menu_proof.py --mutant browser-export-failed-enabled   # R1 → M34

271	**Core mutants.** Each is run once, as a single replacement in a scratch copy of `core/` and `graphic/` (the precedent is the README's paste-graphic section). The cargo failure each causes is recorded in `tools/proof/README.md`.
272	- `usage-no-fallback`: a fallback face is not recorded. Caught by `usage.rs`'s fallback test.
273	- `usage-bad-asset`: a non-image asset is recorded. Caught by `usage.rs`.
274	- `crc-init-zero`: the CRC starts from 0. Caught by `graphic_package.rs`'s CRC test.
275	- `legal-keep-colon`: `:` is left out of the legaliser's set. Caught by `graphic_package.rs`'s in-package-name test.
276	- `legal-no-suffix`: a claimed legalised name takes no `-N`. Caught by the collision case of the same test.

278	**Passing means:**
279	- `make gate` exits 0 with exactly the 4 baseline warnings.
280	- Each proof ends `<n>/<n> checks passed`.
281	- `grep "Frame Job: " <dir>/framejob.log` prints nothing.
282	- All 9 mutants are caught under their rule: R1, its own row fails first; R, exit 0; core, its named test fails.
283	- `wc -l app/Sources/ReelCore.swift` is ≤ 788.

285	## Out of scope
286	- Importing or opening a `.fjgraphic`: a `CFBundleDocumentTypes` row, a reader, a "From Package…" button. It is filed at close as a GitHub issue labelled `ai-drafted` and `low-priority`.
287	- Sampling string or asset props beyond their defaults, a caller's own text at render time, and the Mac's installed fonts.
288	- Thumbnails, search, collections of templates, signing or encrypting a package, and Zip64.

291	1. `withByteBuffer` cannot serve the two in-place AV1 sites (`stripTemporalDelimiters`, `brandAV01` take `uint8_t *` and mutate an `inout Data`) — changed, per RULING-1 (1): the mutable twin `withMutableByteBuffer(_ data: inout Data, …)` is added to Interfaces and `CoreValues.swift`, used at those two sites with their in-place writes kept. Re-measured: the seven sites save about 17 lines against about 20 added. So a second payment is named in Approach 4: the `extension ReelOp` docs are cut to their contracts, with the rationale moved word for word into the ADR. It is gated alone, and if the file is still over 788 the implementer stops; the cap is not relaxed.

The manifest gains `name` per file, the project's name, so `asset(name)` resolves after import. `rc_graphic_package_write` now answers the manifest so Swift can report the paths it used. The Graphic dialog gains **Export…** at its far left. It writes the chosen graphic as a `.fjgraphic` zip holding a manifest, the module, and only those project fonts and assets the graphics engine saw it draw or measure with.   - `docs/guide/mcp.md` — "One hundred and one tools", and the row.

  - `docs/guide/menus-and-shortcuts.md` — the Graphic… row names Export….
  - `docs/manual-checks.md` — GR-15.
  - `CONTEXT.md` — the term **Graphic package**.
  - `README.md` — the Motion graphics highlight.

## Interfaces
```rust
// graphic/src/library.rs — Usage is cumulative over every parse and measure against one library
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Usage { pub fonts: Vec<usize>, pub assets: Vec<String> } // blob indexes into new()'s `fonts` (faceless blobs counted), ascending; asset names, sorted
impl Library { pub fn usage(&self) -> Usage }
```
```c
/* {"fonts":[<blob index>…],"assets":[<name>…]}: the font blobs whose faces a parse or measure against
 * `lib` selected (directly or as a fallback), and the image assets it resolved. Freezes it. NULL only for NULL. */
char *rc_graphic_library_usage(const RcGraphicLibrary *lib);
/* Writes the .fjgraphic at `path` (created or truncated). package_json: {"module","title","category",
 * "description":string|null,"app_version","files":[{"path","size"}…]}, each path relative to the project's
 * `graphics/` folder; `data` is the files' bytes concatenated in that order. Answers the manifest.json it wrote
 * (freed with rc_string_free); NULL with a lowercase sentence through err_out, including for a NULL argument. */
char *rc_graphic_package_write(const char *path, const char *package_json, const uint8_t *data, size_t len, char **err_out);
```
**What the core refuses**, each sentence naming the value:
- `module` failing `model_graphic::check_name`.
- `title`, `category` or `app_version` that is not a string, or a `description` that is neither a string nor null.
- A first file that is not exactly `<module>.js`.
- Any other file not `fonts/<n>` or `assets/<n>`, where `<n>` must be non-empty, at most 255 bytes, and hold no `/`. Any other character is legalised, never refused (below).
- A path given twice.
- Sizes that do not sum to `len`.
- An archive over `u32::MAX` bytes (there is no Zip64).
- I/O failures.

**The archive:**
- Stored (method 0), version needed 10, made-by `0x031E`, flag bit 11 (UTF-8 names).
- DOS time 0 and date `0x0021` (1980-01-01), so the bytes are deterministic.
- No extra fields and no directory entries; external attributes `0o100644 << 16`.
- `manifest.json` first, then the files in the order given, then the central directory and the EOCD.

**The in-package name** (G-46 (c)). A legal `<n>` is non-empty, at most 255 bytes, does not begin with `.`, and holds no `/`, `\`, `:` or control scalar (U+0000–U+001F, U+007F–U+009F). The module's entry is always `<module>.js`. For `fonts/` and `assets/`, each folder on its own:
- A legal `<n>` is kept as it is, and the legal names are claimed first, in the order given.
- Then each illegal `<n>`, in the order given, is legalised: each run of `\`, `:` or control scalars becomes one `-`, and leading `.`s are dropped; an empty result is `file`.
- A legalised name already claimed takes `-2`, `-3`, … before its last `.` (G-23 (c)'s form), the stem cut by whole scalars to stay within 255 bytes.
- `a:b.ttf` → `fonts/a-b.ttf`; `red\dot.png` → `assets/red-dot.png`; `a:b.ttf` beside a legal `a-b.ttf` → `fonts/a-b-2.ttf`.

**`manifest.json`** is pretty JSON with a trailing newline, in this key order: `{"fjgraphic": 1, "module", "title", "category", "description", "app_version", "files": [{"path", "name", "size", "sha256"}…]}`. `path` is the in-package path; `name` is the file's name in its project folder (`<module>.js`, the font's, the asset's), which is how a module's `asset(name)` still resolves after a renamed entry is imported. `sha256` is lowercase hex, and the manifest does not list itself.
```swift
func withByteBuffer<R>(_ data: Data, _ body: (UnsafePointer<UInt8>?, Int) -> R) -> R   // CoreValues: exactly the inline withUnsafeBytes/bindMemory it replaces
func withMutableByteBuffer<R>(_ data: inout Data, _ body: (UnsafeMutablePointer<UInt8>?, Int) -> R) -> R   // CoreValues: exactly the inline withUnsafeMutableBytes/bindMemory it replaces (in place)
struct GraphicUsage: Equatable { let fonts: [Int]; let assets: [String]; static func decoded(_ json: String?) -> GraphicUsage }  // CoreValues; empty on nil/unreadable
func usage() -> GraphicUsage                                              // GraphicLibrary (ReelCore)
enum ReelGraphicPackage { static func write(path: String, packageJSON: String, data: Data) throws -> String }  // ReelCore; the manifest's text; ReelCoreError(core's sentence)
static func bundledFontURLs(in folder: URL) -> [URL]                      // GraphicStore: .ttf/.otf sorted by name, what makeLibrary adds first
func makeIndexedLibrary() throws -> (library: GraphicLibrary, fonts: [GraphicFile?], scan: GraphicScan)  // fonts[i] nil = bundled blob i
enum GraphicPackage {
    static let fileExtension = "fjgraphic", typeIdentifier = "com.kgalligan.framejob-graphic"
    static let maxFrames = 900, variantFrames = 30, maxVariants = 32
    static var contentType: UTType   // UTType(typeIdentifier) ?? UTType(filenameExtension: fileExtension, conformingTo: .zip) ?? .zip
    static var appVersion: String    // CFBundleShortVersionString, else ""
    static func sampledFrames(length: Int, cap: Int) -> [Int]  // 0..<length if length ≤ cap, else round(i·(length−1)/(cap−1)) for i in 0..<cap
}
struct GraphicPackageResult { let url: URL; let files: [String]; let frames: Int; let failedFrames: Int }  // files: the manifest's in-package paths, after manifest.json
struct GraphicPackageJob {
    static func project(named: String, document: ProjectDocument) throws -> GraphicPackageJob  // main
    static func template(_ entry: GraphicTemplateLibrary.Entry, document: ProjectDocument) throws -> GraphicPackageJob  // main
    func write(to url: URL) throws -> GraphicPackageResult   // never main, never GCD; the sheet's 8 MiB Thread or the agent's server thread
}
// GraphicBrowserSheetController: identifier "graphicbrowser.export"; func exportChosen(to url: URL) (internal; the panel's OK; the probe's entry)
func exportGraphic(_ a: [String: Any]) throws -> String   // AgentServer — UI path: Insert ▸ Graphic…'s Export…
```
**`export_graphic`.** Its arguments are `{name: string, from: "template"|"project", path: string}`, all required. Like `render_graphic`, it is in `offMainTools` and has no `scope`.
- **The path:** `nonEmptyOutputPath`, then `destinationURL(_, extension: "fjgraphic")`, then `requireFolder`. An existing file is replaced.
- **The reply:** `{"path", "files": ["manifest.json", …], "frames", "failed_frames"}`, `files` being the in-package paths.
- **Refusals:** `from` and an unknown name are refused as `insert_graphic` refuses them. A project module that does not compile gets G-45 (f)'s sentence. A refusal writes nothing and leaves no `.partial` file.
- **The ask-first reason:** "It writes a .fjgraphic package where the model chose, replacing any file already there."

## Approach
1. **Spec §11 G-46, written before any code, in `graphics.md` with its README row.**
   - **(a) The door.** Export… sits at the sheet's far left, with From File… to its right. It is enabled when a graphic is chosen and compiles. It opens an `NSSavePanel` as a sheet on the browser, named `<module>.fjgraphic`. The browser stays up; the result or the refusal goes in `graphicbrowser.message`.
   - **(b) The usage rule.**
     - Build a fresh library: the bundled faces, then the project's fonts, then its assets. Compile the module against it.
     - Draw each frame (svg, then rasterize at the meta size, else the canvas) with default props. That is every frame up to 900; past that, 900 evenly spaced frames.
     - Then draw the variants, one at a time with every other prop at its default: each `enum` option other than the default, and each boolean's opposite. Take them in schema order, at most 32, over 30 evenly spaced frames each.
     - Pack every project font blob and asset the engine selected, measured, fell back to or resolved. A bundled face is never packed.
     - A frame that throws is skipped and counted. String and asset props are sampled only at their defaults.
   - **(c) The format,** as in Interfaces. Its paths mirror `graphics/`, so a later import is a copy. A project font or asset whose name the package path cannot hold (`\`, `:`, a control character, a leading `.`) is never refused at export: the core legalises its in-package name by Interfaces' rule, and the manifest's `name` keeps the project's, so an import can restore it and `asset(name)` still resolves. A font is found by family, never by file name, so its renamed entry changes no picture.
   - **(d) The UTI** is exported only; the app does not open a `.fjgraphic`.
   - **(e) `export_graphic`** runs off main, and is ask-first under AI-7's own criterion: it writes a file where the model chose.
   - **(f) Import is not built.** It is filed as an issue when the phase closes.
2. **The graphic crate.** Each closure calls usvg first — `select_font`, the fallback selector or `image_kind` — and only afterwards locks the usage set, for its own insert, because a nested SVG asset re-enters on the same thread. `tests/usage.rs`, with `common::fonts()`, checks:
   - Anton drawn records Anton's index; `serif` records Source Serif 4's; a missing family records nothing.
   - A fallback records both faces. Use a character Anton lacks: drawn in a library of Anton alone it draws nothing, and in Anton + Source Sans 3 it draws.
   - `measure_text` alone records its face.
   - A drawn PNG href is recorded; a non-image asset and a missing href are not.
   - A nested SVG asset's text records its face.
   - A faceless blob at index 0 moves Anton to index 1.
   - Usage accumulates across calls and is separate per library.
3. **The core.**
   - The CRC is CRC-32 IEEE: a reflected table, with init and xorout `0xFFFFFFFF`.
   - `tests/graphic_package.rs` uses its own zip reader (EOCD → central directory → local headers), a bitwise CRC (the check value `"123456789"` → `0xCBF43926`) and `sha2`. It checks:
     - each entry's order and bytes, its CRC, both size fields, flag bit 11 and the 1980 date;
     - the manifest's text, its key order and its checksums;
     - that two writes are byte-identical;
     - each refusal, with nothing written for an input refusal;
     - the in-package names: `fonts/a:b.ttf` → `fonts/a-b.ttf`, `assets/red\dot.png` → `assets/red-dot.png`, a control-character run → one `-`, a leading `.` dropped, `fonts/:` → `fonts/-`, `fonts/..` → `fonts/file`; `fonts/a:b.ttf` given before a legal `fonts/a-b.ttf` still yields `a-b.ttf` for the legal one and `a-b-2.ttf` for the renamed one; each manifest `name` is the given name; a legal name is unchanged.
   - Finish with `cargo fmt` and `make lint`.
4. **The ReelCore toll, landed and gated alone.**
   - **Payment 1, the byte-buffer helpers.** Add `withByteBuffer` and `withMutableByteBuffer` to `CoreValues.swift`. Rewrite the seven inline sites in `ReelCore.swift`: `withByteBuffer` at `ReelAV1.config`, `ReelWebM.add`/`addVideo`, `GraphicLibrary.addFont`/`addAsset`; `withMutableByteBuffer(&data)` at `ReelAV1.stripTemporalDelimiters` and `withMutableByteBuffer(&head)` at `ReelAV1.brandAV01`, which keep writing in place. The pointers, their mutability and the `rc_*` calls stay the same; no `UnsafeMutablePointer(mutating:)` anywhere.
   - **Payment 2, the `extension ReelOp` docs.** These seven sites save about 17 lines; `usage()` and `ReelGraphicPackage` add about 20. So `coreSchemas()`'s and `coreNames()`'s docs are cut to their contracts: what each answers, where it comes from (`rc_op_schemas` / `rc_op_names`), and that empty means the core failed. Their rationale paragraphs go word for word into the `ReelCore.swift` entry of `app-file-history.md`: why the FFI rather than a Swift copy, why empty is a catastrophe, and why the member stayed in this file. No code changes.
   - Each payment is a pure change, gated alone by `make typecheck` (0 errors, the 4 baseline warnings), and recorded with its before and after `wc -l`.
   - Only then add `usage()` and `ReelGraphicPackage`. If the file is still over 788 after them, stop and report it; do not relax the cap.
5. **`GraphicStore` and `GraphicPackageJob`.**
   - **The factories** read:
     - the meta: title, category and description through `GraphicCatalog`; the size and the length through `AgentServer.metaWhole`, as `render_graphic` does;
     - the module's bytes: `scan.modules[name].bytes`, or the template's file;
     - the library: `makeIndexedLibrary()`. A template gets a library of `bundledFontURLs` alone: every entry nil, no assets.
   - **`write`:**
     1. Compile at `GraphicRegistry.offlineBudgetMs`. A failure is G-45 (f)'s sentence, labelled `graphics/<name>.js` or `the template "<name>"`.
     2. Draw 1(b)'s frames through `AgentServer.graphicContext`. The variants come from `GraphicSchema(describeJSON:schema:)`.
     3. Map the usage to files: a font index to `fonts/<its file name>`, an asset to `assets/<name>`, both as project-relative paths. The core picks the in-package names; `GraphicPackageResult.files` is read from the manifest it answers.
     4. Write `.<file>.partial` beside the destination with `ReelGraphicPackage.write`, then move it into place, replacing an existing file. Any throw removes the partial file.
6. **The sheet.**
   - The Export… button (a `.secondary` `StickerButton`) goes first in `leading:`. It is enabled when `chosenItem?.ok == true` and no export is running.
   - `exportClicked` opens the save panel: `allowedContentTypes` is `[GraphicPackage.contentType]` and the name `<module>.fjgraphic`, shown with `beginSheetModal(for: view.window)`. OK calls `exportChosen(to:)`.
   - `exportChosen(to:)` builds the job on main. A throw beeps and shows the sentence.
   - Otherwise it shows "Exporting <title>…" and runs `write` on a `Thread` with `stackSize = GraphicPrefetch.workerStackBytes`.
   - On main (`[weak self]`) it shows "Exported <title> to <file name>: <files joined by ", ">.", or else the sentence with a beep, and re-enables Export….
   - No edit and no undo step.
7. **The agent side.**
   - `exportGraphic` resolves the graphic through `browserGraphic` and builds the job inside `onMain`, then runs `write` on the server thread.
   - Then the wiring: the catalog row, the handler row, the off-main row, the ask-first row with its `question` case, and the prompt topic.
   - Then the counts and docs: the spec, the screen file, the ADR and the inventory.
   - **GR-15** is a person's check:
     - the save panel shows as a sheet on the dialog, in both appearances;
     - the message reads whole;
     - Finder shows the Kind "Frame Job Graphic";
     - Archive Utility unpacks it to `manifest.json` and the module, with `fonts/` and `assets/` only when they are used.
8. **Proofs.**
   - **The probe:**
     - **M33:** Export… is the leftmost bottom-bar button (its `minX` < `graphicbrowser.fromFile`'s), titled "Export…", and enabled on the opening graphic.
     - **M34:** it is disabled with no graphic chosen, and on a This Project module that does not compile.
     - **M35:** on Titles & Text ▸ Lower third, pressing it attaches an `NSSavePanel` to the browser window within 2 s, named `lower-third.fjgraphic`, with the browser still up; the panel is then cancelled.
     - **M36:** `exportChosen(to:)` writes a file beginning `PK\x03\x04` within 30 s, and the message reads "Exported Lower third to <name>: lower-third.js.".
     - **M37:** through M35–M36 the browser stays up, the project handle and the undo count are unchanged, and the export thread has finished.
   - **`graphic_browser_proof.py`:**
     - **E0:**
       - `import_graphic_font` of `/System/Library/Fonts/Supplemental/Arial.ttf` and `Georgia.ttf`; a missing file is a FAIL.
       - `import_graphic_asset` of `graphic/tests/assets/red.png` and `steel.jpg`.
       - Module `late-font` (durationInFrames 90): Source Sans 3 throughout, Arial only from frame 60, and an image from an `asset` prop whose default is `red.png`.
       - Module `variant`: an enum `face`, default `sans`, options `[sans, georgia]`, drawing in Georgia only for `georgia`.
       - Module `broken`.
     - **E1:** exporting `late-font` from the project answers a `.fjgraphic` path. With Python's `zipfile` and `hashlib` as the oracle:
       - `testzip()` is None;
       - the names are exactly `[manifest.json, late-font.js, fonts/Arial.ttf, assets/red.png]`, all `ZIP_STORED`;
       - each entry's bytes equal the package's file;
       - the manifest's keys, their order and their values are as specified: `app_version` is the bundle's `CFBundleShortVersionString`, and each `sha256` is the file's.
     - **E2:** `variant` holds `fonts/Georgia.ttf` and no other font.
     - **E3:** the `lower-third` template holds exactly `manifest.json` and a `lower-third.js` byte-equal to the bundled one. No package has a `fonts/` entry byte-equal to an `app/Resources/Fonts` file.
     - **E4:** re-exporting E1 to the same path replaces the file with identical bytes, and a path with no extension gains `.fjgraphic`.
     - **E5:** `from: file`, an unknown name, `broken` and a missing folder are each refused, leaving nothing at the path and no `.partial`.
     - **E6:** `/System/Library/Fonts/Supplemental/Verdana.ttf` is copied to a scratch `Ver:dana.ttf` and imported, and `red.png` is copied to `red\dot.png` and imported (G-23 keeps that name; the reply has no `renamed_from`). Module `odd-names` draws Verdana text and `asset("red\\dot.png")`. Its export:
       - is not refused;
       - holds `fonts/Ver-dana.ttf` and `assets/red-dot.png`, each byte-equal to its project file;
       - has manifest entries whose `name` is `Ver:dana.ttf` and `red\dot.png`.

## Constraints
- **The graphic crate:** `graphic/src` files stay under 400 lines, with no fs, env or net, and `forbid(unsafe_code)`.
- **The core:**
  - Only `ffi_graphic.rs` names `graphic` (`graphic_ffi.rs`'s scan).
  - Every new export has a `///` contract and a `# Safety` paragraph, puts NULL tolerance first, goes through `ffi_util.rs`, and is in the null sweep.
  - Tests are black-box with independent oracles.
  - No format bump, since nothing persisted changes.
- **The FFI lockstep:** Rust, the header, then `ReelCore.swift`, the only `rc_*` caller. The toll comes before any addition.
- **Threads:** QuickJS runs only on the sheet's 8 MiB `Thread` or the agent's server thread. AppKit and the document are touched on main only (`onMain` for the tool).
- **Frozen and capped files:** `AgentServer.swift` is frozen and takes wiring only. New files are ≤ 400 lines, and no listed file crosses 600.
- **Typecheck:** 0 errors and the 4 baseline warnings.
- **Refusals:** the sheet and the tool use the same sentences, and `insert_graphic`'s are unchanged.
- **The assistant prompt:** `assistant_prompt_proof.py --probe`'s F4–F8 must hold (system ≤ 6000, guide ≤ 1500).
- **Proof hygiene:** no persisting menu item; scratch homes only.
- **Decisions:** G-16, G-45 and AI-7 are not re-litigated.
- **CLAUDE.md edits owed** (for the orchestrator; listed in the notes, not made here):
  - root: "one hundred and one", and `export_graphic` in the app-state list;
  - `core/`: map entries, and `sha2` as a dependency;
  - `graphic/`: the usage recorder and its lock rule;
  - `app/`: map entries (`GraphicPackage.swift`, the sheet's export, `makeIndexedLibrary`, `ReelGraphicPackage`/`usage`, `withByteBuffer`/`withMutableByteBuffer`/`GraphicUsage`), the thread-seam list, and the counts.

## Verification
Targeted (run while iterating; covers only the code in **Files**):
```
cd graphic && cargo test --release --test usage
cd core && cargo test --release --test graphic_package
cd core && cargo test --release --test graphic_ffi
cd core && cargo test --release --test model_tests null_safety
make lint
make typecheck
python3 tools/proof/capture_spike/inventory.py --check
python3 tools/proof/spec_index_proof.py
python3 tools/proof/assistant_prompt_proof.py --probe
make app-debug && python3 tools/proof/graphics_menu_proof.py
python3 tools/proof/graphic_browser_proof.py
```
Full (run once, after the targeted checks pass; only commands the files in **Files** can affect):
```
make gate      # names, typecheck, fmt, lint, test, Release app — the one Full command (CLAUDE.md)
RC_PROOF_APP=release python3 tools/proof/graphics_menu_proof.py     # covers: Export… in the sheet (M33–M37)
RC_PROOF_APP=release python3 tools/proof/graphic_browser_proof.py   # covers: export_graphic's package, the usage rule, legalised names, refusals, ten identifiers
python3 tools/proof/op_argument_proof.py <dir>/agent.sock          # covers: 101 product tools, the gate on export_graphic (Release instance, proof_app.py launch --app release)
python3 tools/proof/phase9_proof.py <dir>/agent.sock               # covers: the exact app-state tool set
python3 tools/proof/graphics_menu_proof.py --mutant browser-export-failed-enabled   # R1 → M34
python3 tools/proof/graphic_browser_proof.py --mutant export-frame-zero    # only frame 0 sampled → E1 (rule R)
python3 tools/proof/graphic_browser_proof.py --mutant export-all-assets    # every asset packed → E1
python3 tools/proof/graphic_browser_proof.py --mutant export-no-variants   # variants skipped → E2
```
**Core mutants.** Each is run once, as a single replacement in a scratch copy of `core/` and `graphic/` (the precedent is the README's paste-graphic section). The cargo failure each causes is recorded in `tools/proof/README.md`.
- `usage-no-fallback`: a fallback face is not recorded. Caught by `usage.rs`'s fallback test.
- `usage-bad-asset`: a non-image asset is recorded. Caught by `usage.rs`.
- `crc-init-zero`: the CRC starts from 0. Caught by `graphic_package.rs`'s CRC test.
- `legal-keep-colon`: `:` is left out of the legaliser's set. Caught by `graphic_package.rs`'s in-package-name test.
- `legal-no-suffix`: a claimed legalised name takes no `-N`. Caught by the collision case of the same test.

**Passing means:**
- `make gate` exits 0 with exactly the 4 baseline warnings.
- Each proof ends `<n>/<n> checks passed`.
- `grep "Frame Job: " <dir>/framejob.log` prints nothing.
- All 9 mutants are caught under their rule: R1, its own row fails first; R, exit 0; core, its named test fails.
- `wc -l app/Sources/ReelCore.swift` is ≤ 788.

## Out of scope
- Importing or opening a `.fjgraphic`: a `CFBundleDocumentTypes` row, a reader, a "From Package…" button. It is filed at close as a GitHub issue labelled `ai-drafted` and `low-priority`.
- Sampling string or asset props beyond their defaults, a caller's own text at render time, and the Mac's installed fonts.
- Thumbnails, search, collections of templates, signing or encrypting a package, and Zip64.

## Objections addressed
1. `withByteBuffer` cannot serve the two in-place AV1 sites (`stripTemporalDelimiters`, `brandAV01` take `uint8_t *` and mutate an `inout Data`) — changed, per RULING-1 (1): the mutable twin `withMutableByteBuffer(_ data: inout Data, …)` is added to Interfaces and `CoreValues.swift`, used at those two sites with their in-place writes kept. Re-measured: the seven sites save about 17 lines against about 20 added. So a second payment is named in Approach 4: the `extension ReelOp` docs are cut to their contracts, with the rationale moved word for word into the ADR. It is gated alone, and if the file is still over 788 the implementer stops; the cap is not relaxed.
2. RULING-1 (2), a project font (or asset: G-23 allows `\`) whose name holds a character the package path refuses — legalise, not refuse. The core legalises each in-package name (runs of `\`, `:` or control characters become `-`, a leading `.` is dropped, collisions take G-23 (c)'s `-N`). The manifest gains `name` per file, the project's name, so `asset(name)` resolves after import. `rc_graphic_package_write` now answers the manifest so Swift can report the paths it used. Recorded in G-46 (c); `graphic_package.rs` cases, proof row E6, and two core mutants (`legal-keep-colon`, `legal-no-suffix`) replace `path-leading-dot`.

1	// app/Sources/GraphicPackage.swift — the Graphic dialog's Export… and
2	// `export_graphic` (spec §11 G-46): one graphic written as a `.fjgraphic`
3	// package holding its module and only the project fonts and assets the
4	// engine saw it use.
5	//
6	// **A job is built on main and written off it.** `GraphicPackageJob.project`
7	// and `.template` read the document on main: the module's bytes, its title,
8	// category and description (`GraphicCatalog`), its size and length
9	// (`AgentServer.metaWhole`, as `render_graphic` reads them), and a FRESH
10	// library (`GraphicStore.makeIndexedLibrary()`; a template's holds the
11	// bundled faces alone). `write(to:)` runs QuickJS, so it runs only on the
12	// sheet's 8 MiB `Thread` or the agent's server thread — never main, never GCD.
13	//
14	// **The usage rule** (G-46 (b)): the module is compiled against that library
15	// and drawn — every frame up to `maxFrames` with its default props, else
16	// `maxFrames` evenly spaced, each `svg` then `rasterize` — and then each
17	// variant (an `enum` option other than the default, a boolean's opposite, in
18	// schema order, at most `maxVariants`) over `variantFrames` evenly spaced
19	// frames, every other prop at its default. The library's `usage()` is then
20	// every project font blob and asset to pack; a bundled face never is. A
21	// frame that throws is skipped and counted.
22	//
23	// **The file** is the core's (`ReelGraphicPackage.write`): written as
24	// `.<file>.partial` beside the destination and renamed over it, so an
25	// existing file is replaced whole; any throw removes the partial file.
26	
27	import Foundation
28	import UniformTypeIdentifiers
29	
30	enum GraphicPackage {
31	    static let fileExtension = "fjgraphic", typeIdentifier = "com.kgalligan.framejob-graphic"
32	    static let maxFrames = 900, variantFrames = 30, maxVariants = 32
33	
34	    /// The exported type (`project.yml`), else a zip by its extension.
35	    static var contentType: UTType {
36	        UTType(typeIdentifier)
37	            ?? UTType(filenameExtension: fileExtension, conformingTo: .zip) ?? .zip
38	    }
39	
40	    /// The manifest's `app_version`: the bundle's `CFBundleShortVersionString`, else "".
41	    static var appVersion: String {
42	        Bundle.main.object(forInfoDictionaryKey: "CFBundleShortVersionString") as? String ?? ""
43	    }
44	
45	    /// Every frame of `length` when there are at most `cap`, else `cap` frames evenly spaced
46	    /// from the first to the last.
47	    static func sampledFrames(length: Int, cap: Int) -> [Int] {
48	        guard length > cap else { return Array(0..<max(length, 0)) }
49	        guard cap > 1 else { return cap == 1 ? [0] : [] }
50	        return (0..<cap).map { i in
51	            Int((Double(i) * Double(length - 1) / Double(cap - 1)).rounded())
52	        }
53	    }
54	
55	    /// The props of each variant G-46 (b) draws: one per `enum` option other than its
56	    /// default and one per boolean's opposite, in schema order, at most `maxVariants`.
57	    static func variants(_ schema: GraphicSchema) -> [[String: Any]] {
58	        var out: [[String: Any]] = []
59	        for entry in schema.entries {
60	            switch (entry.type, entry.default) {
61	            case ("enum", let value):
62	                let current: String? = { if case .string(let s) = value { return s }; return nil }()
63	                for option in entry.options where option != current {
64	                    out.append([entry.key: option])
65	                }
66	            case ("boolean", .bool(let flag)):
67	                out.append([entry.key: !flag])
68	            default:
69	                continue
70	            }
71	        }
72	        return Array(out.prefix(maxVariants))
73	    }
74	}
75	
76	/// What one export wrote.
77	struct GraphicPackageResult {
78	    let url: URL
79	    /// The manifest's in-package paths, in order; `manifest.json` itself is not among them.
80	    let files: [String]
81	    /// Every frame drawn (the defaults' and the variants'), and how many of them threw.
82	    let frames: Int
83	    let failedFrames: Int
84	}
85	
86	/// One graphic, read off the document on main, ready to be written off it.
87	struct GraphicPackageJob {
88	    let name: String
89	    /// What a compile failure names: `graphics/<name>.js` or `the template "<name>"`.
90	    let label: String
91	    let title: String
92	    let category: String
93	    let description: String?
94	    let source: Data
95	    let library: GraphicLibrary
96	    /// The library's font blobs: the project file each came from, nil for a bundled face.
97	    let fonts: [GraphicFile?]
98	    let assets: [GraphicFile]
99	    let width: Int
100	    let height: Int
101	    let length: Int
102	    let fps: Fps
103	    let canvas: CanvasSnapshot
104	    let appVersion: String
105	
106	    /// A This Project module, read on main. Throws the store's sentence when the folder does
107	    /// not hold it.
108	    static func project(named name: String, document: ProjectDocument) throws -> GraphicPackageJob {
109	        guard let store = document.graphicStore else {
110	            throw ReelCoreError(message: ProjectDocument.noGraphicsFolderSentence)
111	        }
112	        let indexed = try store.makeIndexedLibrary()
113	        guard let file = indexed.scan.modules[name] else {
114	            throw ReelCoreError(message: store.noModuleSentence(name))
115	        }
116	        var meta: [String: Any] = [:]
117	        if case .compiled(_, _, let described, _)? = GraphicRegistry.shared.entry(
118	            named: name, for: document.recipeKey)
119	        {
120	            meta = described
121	        }
122	        return try make(
123	            name: name, label: "graphics/\(name).js", meta: meta, source: file.bytes,
124	            library: indexed.library, fonts: indexed.fonts, assets: indexed.scan.assets,
125	            document: document)
126	    }
127	
128	    /// A bundled template, read on main, with a library of the bundled faces alone.
129	    static func template(
130	        _ entry: GraphicTemplateLibrary.Entry, document: ProjectDocument
131	    ) throws -> GraphicPackageJob {
132	        let name = entry.template.name
133	        let source: Data
134	        do {
135	            source = try Data(contentsOf: entry.template.url)
136	        } catch {
137	            throw ReelCoreError(
138	                message: "\(entry.template.url.path) could not be read: "
139	                    + error.localizedDescription)
140	        }
141	        let library = GraphicLibrary()
142	        var fonts: [GraphicFile?] = []
143	        for url in GraphicStore.bundledFontURLs(in: ProjectDocument.bundledFontsDirectory) {
144	            try library.addFont(Data(contentsOf: url))
145	            fonts.append(nil)
146	        }
147	        var meta: [String: Any] = [:]
148	        if case .compiled(_, _, let described, _) = entry.entry { meta = described }
149	        return try make(
150	            name: name, label: "the template \"\(name)\"", meta: meta, source: source,
151	            library: library, fonts: fonts, assets: [], document: document)
152	    }
153	
154	    private static func make(
155	        name: String, label: String, meta: [String: Any], source: Data, library: GraphicLibrary,
156	        fonts: [GraphicFile?], assets: [GraphicFile], document: ProjectDocument
157	    ) throws -> GraphicPackageJob {
158	        let canvas = document.project.snapshot.canvas
159	        let tick = max(canvas.fps.frameDuration, 1)
160	        let width: Int, height: Int, length: Int
161	        do {
162	            width = try AgentServer.metaWhole(meta, "width", name, in: AgentServer.sides)
163	                ?? canvas.width
164	            height = try AgentServer.metaWhole(meta, "height", name, in: AgentServer.sides)
165	                ?? canvas.height
166	            length = try AgentServer.metaWhole(
167	                meta, "durationInFrames", name, in: 1...Int.max / Int(tick))
168	                ?? Int((5 * canvas.fps.double).rounded(.up))
169	        } catch let error as AgentServer.ToolError {
170	            throw ReelCoreError(message: error.message)
171	        }
172	        return GraphicPackageJob(
173	            name: name, label: label, title: GraphicCatalog.title(meta: meta, name: name),
174	            category: GraphicCatalog.category(meta: meta),
175	            description: GraphicCatalog.description(meta: meta), source: source,
176	            library: library, fonts: fonts, assets: assets, width: width, height: height,
177	            length: length, fps: canvas.fps, canvas: canvas, appVersion: GraphicPackage.appVersion)
178	    }
179	
180	    /// Compiles, draws by G-46 (b)'s rule, and writes the package at `url`, replacing a file
181	    /// there. Never on main and never on GCD: the sheet's 8 MiB `Thread` or the agent's server
182	    /// thread. Throws a sentence, writing nothing, for a module that does not compile.
183	    func write(to url: URL) throws -> GraphicPackageResult {
184	        let module: GraphicModule
185	        do {
186	            module = try GraphicModule.compile(
187	                library: library, name: name, source: String(decoding: source, as: UTF8.self),
188	                budgetMs: GraphicRegistry.offlineBudgetMs)
189	        } catch {
190	            let first = GraphicDiagnostic.of(error).first
191	            let line = first?.line.map { " (line \($0))" } ?? ""
192	            throw ReelCoreError(
193	                message: "\(label) does not compile: " + (first?.message ?? "no diagnostic")
194	                    + line)
195	        }
196	        let describe = module.describeJSON()
197	        let described = (try? JSONSerialization.jsonObject(with: Data(describe.utf8)))
198	            as? [String: Any]
199	        let schema = GraphicSchema(
200	            describeJSON: describe, schema: described?["schema"] as? [String: Any] ?? [:])
201	        var frames = 0, failed = 0
202	        let sample = { (frame: Int, props: [String: Any]) in
203	            frames += 1
204	            if !self.draw(module, frame: frame, props: props) { failed += 1 }
205	        }
206	        for frame in GraphicPackage.sampledFrames(length: length, cap: GraphicPackage.maxFrames) {
207	            sample(frame, [:])
208	        }
209	        let variantFrames = GraphicPackage.sampledFrames(
210	            length: length, cap: GraphicPackage.variantFrames)
211	        for props in GraphicPackage.variants(schema) {
212	            for frame in variantFrames { sample(frame, props) }
213	        }
214	
215	        let usage = library.usage()
216	        let usedFonts = usage.fonts.compactMap { fonts.indices.contains($0) ? fonts[$0] : nil }
217	        let usedAssets = usage.assets.compactMap { used in assets.first { $0.name == used } }
218	        var listed: [[String: Any]] = [["path": "\(name).js", "size": source.count]]
219	        var data = source
220	        for (folder, files) in [
221	            (GraphicStore.fontsFolderName, usedFonts), (GraphicStore.assetsFolderName, usedAssets),
222	        ] {
223	            for file in files {
224	                listed.append(["path": "\(folder)/\(file.name)", "size": file.bytes.count])
225	                data.append(file.bytes)
226	            }
227	        }
228	        let spec: [String: Any] = [
229	            "module": name, "title": title, "category": category,
230	            "description": description ?? NSNull(), "app_version": appVersion, "files": listed,
231	        ]
232	        let specJSON = String(
233	            decoding: try JSONSerialization.data(withJSONObject: spec), as: UTF8.self)
234	
235	        let partial = url.deletingLastPathComponent()
236	            .appendingPathComponent(".\(url.lastPathComponent).partial")
237	        let manifest: String
238	        do {
239	            manifest = try ReelGraphicPackage.write(
240	                path: partial.path, packageJSON: specJSON, data: data)
241	            guard rename(partial.path, url.path) == 0 else {
242	                let why = String(cString: strerror(errno))
243	                throw ReelCoreError(message: "\(url.path) could not be replaced: \(why)")
244	            }
245	        } catch {
246	            try? FileManager.default.removeItem(at: partial)
247	            throw error
248	        }
249	        let parsed = (try? JSONSerialization.jsonObject(with: Data(manifest.utf8)))
250	            as? [String: Any]
251	        let paths = (parsed?["files"] as? [[String: Any]] ?? [])
252	            .compactMap { $0["path"] as? String }
253	        return GraphicPackageResult(url: url, files: paths, frames: frames, failedFrames: failed)
254	    }
255	
256	    /// One frame drawn and rasterized at the graphic's size; false when either threw.
257	    private func draw(_ module: GraphicModule, frame: Int, props: [String: Any]) -> Bool {
258	        let ctx = AgentServer.graphicContext(
259	            frame: frame, fps: fps, length: length, width: width, height: height, canvas: canvas)
260	        guard let ctxData = try? JSONSerialization.data(withJSONObject: ctx),
261	            let propsData = try? JSONSerialization.data(withJSONObject: props)
262	        else { return false }
263	        do {
264	            let drawn = try module.svg(
265	                frame: frame, propsJSON: String(decoding: propsData, as: UTF8.self),
266	                ctxJSON: String(decoding: ctxData, as: UTF8.self),
267	                budgetMs: GraphicRegistry.offlineBudgetMs)
268	            _ = try library.rasterize(drawn.svg, width: width, height: height)
269	            return true
270	        } catch {
271	            return false
272	        }
273	    }
274	}

content.content:
**The export rows** (G-46), on the same project, after I5. Python's
`zipfile` and `hashlib` are the oracle; each package is read whole.
E0  `import_graphic_font` of `/System/Library/Fonts/Supplemental/Arial.ttf`
    and `Georgia.ttf` (a missing file is a FAIL), `import_graphic_asset` of
    `graphic/tests/assets/red.png` and `steel.jpg`; modules `late-font` (90
    frames: Source Sans 3 throughout, Arial only from frame 60, and an image
    from an `asset` prop whose default is `red.png`), `variant` (an enum
    `face`, default `sans`, options `[sans, georgia]`, Georgia only for
    `georgia`; a boolean `tag`, default false, Arial only when true) and
    `broken`, each written ok;
E1  `export_graphic {late-font, project}` answers a `.fjgraphic` path and 90
    frames, none failed; `testzip()` is None; the entries are exactly
    `[manifest.json, late-font.js, fonts/Arial.ttf, assets/red.png]`, all
    `ZIP_STORED`, each byte-equal to its package file; the reply's `files`
    are the entries; the manifest's keys are `fjgraphic, module, title,
    category, description, app_version, files` in that order (1, late-font,
    "Late font", Other, null, the bundle's `CFBundleShortVersionString`),
    each file's keys `path, name, size, sha256` with the file's own size and
    SHA-256;
E2  `variant`'s package holds `fonts/Arial.ttf` (the boolean variant's) and
    `fonts/Georgia.ttf` (the enum variant's) and no other font;
E3  the `lower-third` template's holds exactly `manifest.json` and a
    `lower-third.js` byte-equal to the bundled one; no package has a
    `fonts/` entry byte-equal to an `app/Resources/Fonts` file;
E4  E1 exported again to the same path leaves identical bytes, and a path
    with no extension gains `.fjgraphic`;
E5  `from: file`, an unknown name, `broken` and a missing folder are each
    refused (the first three in `insert_graphic`'s and G-45 (f)'s
    sentences), leaving nothing at the path and no `.partial` beside it;
E6  Verdana copied to a scratch `Ver:dana.ttf` and imported, `red.png`
    copied to `red\\dot.png` and imported (kept: no `renamed_from`); module
    `odd-names` draws Verdana text and `asset("red\\\\dot.png")`. Its export
    is not refused, holds `fonts/Ver-dana.ttf` and `assets/red-dot.png`, each
    byte-equal to its project file, and the manifest's `name`s are
    `Ver:dana.ttf` and `red\\dot.png`;
U1  (light, then dark on its own instance) `perform_menu_item {path:
    ["Insert", "Graphic…"]}` answers a non-null `sheet`; `snapshot_ui
    {window: sheet}` writes a non-empty PNG and a layout dump holding the
    ten identifiers `graphicbrowser.categories`, `.graphics`, `.preview`,
    `.title`, `.description`, `.message`, `.export`, `.fromFile`, `.cancel`,
    `.insert`, and no layout problem; `cancel_sheet` answers `how: cancel_button` and a null `sheet`, and
    GB's clips are as before;
Z1  every project closes and `grep "Frame Job: "` over each log prints
    nothing.

**The app-tier mutant** (`APP_MUTANTS`): a COPY of the tree
(`tree_copy.make_copy`) with one anchor replaced, built by the copy's own
`make app-debug` (`make app` under `RC_PROOF_APP=release`;
`tree_copy.build_app`), launched in the scratch home, light only. Rule R: exit
0 means its row FAILED in the copy — caught; 1 that it passed — survived; 2
that the control could not be performed (the copy did not build or launch,
or the row was not reached). Each runs the tool and export rows.

+### Sharing a graphic
+
+**Export…** in the Graphic dialog saves the chosen graphic as a
+`.fjgraphic` file (Finder calls it a Frame Job Graphic): a zip holding a
+`manifest.json`, the module, and the project fonts and pictures it uses. It
+is enabled when the chosen graphic compiles. A save panel slides down over
+the dialog, named after the module; the dialog stays open, and the line under
+the lists says "Exporting <title>…", then "Exported <title> to <file>: …"
+with the files it holds, or why it could not. Saving over a file replaces it.
+Exporting changes nothing in the project and is not an undo step.
+
+To find which fonts and pictures belong in the package, Frame Job draws the
+graphic: every frame (up to 900; a longer graphic has 900 frames spread over
+it) with its default properties, then each choice of each `enum` property
+and the other value of each `boolean` property, one at a time, over 30
+frames each (at most 32 of these). A font is packed when the graphic drew or
+measured text with it, or fell back to it for a character its own font
+lacks; a picture when an `asset(name)` drew it. The app's own fonts are
+never packed, since every copy of Frame Job has them. Text and pictures a
+graphic only uses for property values other than the defaults (a different
+title, another picture) are not looked for. A frame that fails is skipped.
+
+A file name a zip path cannot hold (a `:` or `\`, a control character, a
+leading `.`) is stored under a tidied name (`a:b.ttf` as `a-b.ttf`), and the
+manifest keeps the original, so a font is still found by its family and
+`asset(name)` still finds its picture. Frame Job does not open `.fjgraphic`
+files yet.
+
+*Agents:* `export_graphic` (`name`, `from`: `template` or `project`, `path`)
+is Export…; it answers the path, the files in the package, the frames drawn
+and how many failed. The assistant asks before it runs.
+
 ## The Graphic sub-tab
 
 Select a graphic clip and open the inspector's **Clip** tab: its sub-tabs
